NDT training in Spokane, WA: how it works for Spokane employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Spokane technicians and employers is delivered as self-paced online theory with Level III questions answered by an ASNT NDT Level III, followed by hands-on practice in person at the employer's own facility. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Spokane. The training is based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, and your employer is the party that certifies you. We reply within one business day.

Spokane does not depend on a single industry the way a refinery town or a shipyard town does, and that is good news for anyone starting in NDT. The Spokane and Spokane Valley area holds military aircraft support, metals production, power generation, rail, and general fabrication, so a technician who learns visual, magnetic particle, penetrant and ultrasonic work is useful to employers in several different sectors without moving house.

The practical consequence for training is that no single code or customer defines every job. A rolling mill, an Air Force maintenance contractor and a structural steel fabricator will each ask a Spokane technician to follow a different written procedure. The common foundation is the same: understand the method, apply it to a written procedure, and document the result. That foundation is what a good SNT-TC-1A course teaches.

Request a Spokane training quote, and tell us the methods, levels and head-count you have in mind. Anyone planning ahead can also read the NDT training FAQ, the Atlantis training overview and the USA training page.

How to get NDT certified in Spokane: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Certification in Washington follows the same pattern as elsewhere in the United States. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, the employer certifies its own technicians, and the standard is a set of recommended practices that each employer turns into a written practice of its own. Here is the sequence in order.

  1. Find or have an employer with a written practice. A technician in Spokane is certified by the company that employs them, so the first step is a sponsor whose written practice covers the method and level you want. The practice sets the hours, the examinations and the recertification interval.
  2. Complete the formal training. Take the classroom hours the written practice requires. The training-requirements matrix shows the SNT-TC-1A recommended hours for each method, and your Spokane employer may set higher figures.
  3. Log supervised experience. Document the hours a Spokane technician spends performing the method under a certified Level II or III. Experience is usually the slowest part for a new Spokane technician, so start the log from the first day on a job.
  4. Pass the general examination on principles, equipment and terminology for the method.
  5. Pass the specific examination on the procedures, equipment and acceptance standards your Spokane employer really uses.
  6. Pass the practical examination on real specimens, graded by a Level III or a qualified examiner working under one.
  7. Pass the vision examination: near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation at the intervals the written practice sets. The SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker shows what to expect.
  8. Receive certification signed by your Spokane employer.
  9. Recertify at the interval the written practice sets, which SNT-TC-1A recommends should not exceed five years, by examination or documented performance as permitted.

ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, and ASNT NDT Level III examinations) is the alternative if you want a credential that stays with you rather than with an employer. Atlantis prepares candidates for that route too. See ASNT certification.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Spokane technicians

Each course follows the body of knowledge in SNT-TC-1A for its method. Level 1 courses cover the fundamentals and working under supervision, Level 2 courses cover setting up, calibrating, performing and evaluating examinations to a procedure, and Level 3 preparation covers the basic and method examinations for those who will write procedures and examine others.

Method What the course covers Where it is used around Spokane
UT Sound physics, calibration, thickness gauging, straight-beam and angle-beam weld examination Plate and weld checks at fabricators, thickness work at industrial plants and power facilities
RT Exposure technique, image quality, film and digital interpretation, radiation safety basics Pressure piping and weld acceptance where a customer specifies radiography
MT Magnetising methods, field direction, particle application, indication evaluation Structural welds, forgings, rail and heavy-equipment components, surface checks on aircraft support equipment
PT Process control, dwell times, surface preparation, indication interpretation Non-magnetic metals such as aluminium and stainless parts, castings, welds on fabricated assemblies
VT Acuity and lighting, weld profile and discontinuities, measuring tools, reporting The first examination on most jobs: structural steel, piping, tanks, bridges
PAUT Focal laws, encoded scanning, data analysis, flaw sizing (UT Level II first) Thicker welds and corrosion mapping where a specification permits phased array
TOFD Diffraction technique, setup, sizing of weld flaws (UT Level II first) Heavy-section welds on pressure equipment in power and industrial plants

PAUT and TOFD are advanced ultrasonic techniques and are generally taken after UT Level II. Whether they can be used on a given job depends on the customer's specification and the employer's written practice.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Spokane

Ultrasonic testing is the method Spokane employers ask for most once a technician moves beyond visual work, because it finds subsurface problems in plate, welds and castings without taking anything out of service. A Level I course in UT teaches the physics of sound in metal, how a transducer and flaw detector are set up, how to calibrate against a reference block, and how to take thickness readings. Level II adds angle-beam examination of welds, the evaluation of indications against an acceptance standard, and the writing of a clear report.

In Spokane the thickness-gauging side is common at industrial plants and power facilities, where wall loss on piping and vessels is tracked over time, while angle-beam weld work shows up at fabricators building structures to AWS D1.1 or equipment to ASME rules. Practising on plate and pipe welds, and rehearsing setups in the Practical NDT simulator, is the fastest way to build the confidence the practical examination needs. Our ultrasonic testing training page lists what the course covers, and the UT Level 2 practice questions let you test the theory before you sit the exam.

Where NDT technicians work around Spokane

Military aviation support. Fairchild Air Force Base, west of the city, is home to KC-135 aerial refuelling aircraft, and aircraft maintenance, support equipment and base infrastructure all generate inspection work. Military maintenance follows technical orders and contractor quality programmes, and the personnel requirements come from those documents. SNT-TC-1A-based training is a sound foundation, but the employer and its Level III decide how a contract's requirements are met.

Metals and aluminium. The Kaiser Aluminum Trentwood rolling mill in Spokane Valley is one of the larger aluminium flat-rolled operations in North America. Mills of that kind rely on eddy current, ultrasonic and visual methods for product and equipment, and on penetrant and magnetic particle testing for rolls, shafts and structural components.

Power and utilities. Avista Utilities, headquartered in Spokane, operates hydroelectric dams on the Spokane River and gas-fired generation, plus a gas distribution system. Hydro and thermal plants need weld, penstock, pressure-part and structural inspection, much of it to ASME and AWS requirements.

Rail, bridges and structural steel. Spokane sits on major freight rail lines and a regional highway network. Bridge and rail-related steel is examined to AWS D1.5 and AREMA-style owner specifications, with visual and magnetic particle testing doing most of the work.

Fabrication and manufacturing. The Spokane Valley has machine shops, metal fabricators and equipment builders serving mining, timber, agriculture and construction customers across the Northwest. Their customers often require documented NDT personnel qualification, which is where an employer's written practice becomes a sales requirement and not merely a compliance item.

For earnings information on Spokane-area work, see our NDT salary guide, which cites public sources. A technician with multiple methods and a clean record of certification generally has more options than one with a single method.

NDT schools and classes near Spokane: what to compare

Anyone searching for NDT classes in Spokane will find two broad kinds of provider: classroom schools that run scheduled courses at a fixed location, and self-paced programmes that deliver theory online and leave the practical work to the employer. Neither is better in every case. A classroom suits a person with no employer yet who wants hands-on time on specimens before looking for work. Self-paced theory suits someone already employed on shifts, or a company that wants its own staff examined on its own procedures.

Whichever you compare, ask the same questions. Who certifies you when the course ends: the school, or an employer under a written practice? Will the hours count toward the training your future employer's written practice requires? Who grades the practical examination and are they a Level III? What happens if you move to another employer afterwards? A course certificate is evidence of training, and under SNT-TC-1A it is not a certification. Be wary of any provider that implies otherwise.

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Spokane. If you want to learn first and find an employer afterwards, our online theory and the Practical NDT simulator get you ready, and the near-me guide explains how to find a sponsoring employer. If you already have one, the hands-on portion happens at their facility.

Online NDT training in Washington

Technicians in Washington can take the theory for Level I and Level II courses online at their own pace through the Atlantis portal, with Level III Q&A for questions on the material. Access opens the moment you enrol, so a Spokane technician working a rotating schedule can study between shifts. Hands-on training and the practical examination are done in person at your employer's facility, and your employer signs the certification. Details are on the online NDT training page and the Washington training page.

Online theory covers the classroom portion only. The Level III is available to answer questions while you study, and the portal opens the moment you enrol. Courses run year-round, so there is no fixed start date to wait for. Your employer's written practice still decides how many classroom hours count, which is why it helps to ask your Spokane employer before you enrol.

Training a crew at your Spokane facility

A Spokane employer with several technicians to qualify can train the whole group on the same schedule. Theory is self-paced online, so staff do not leave the shop floor for days at a time, and the practical and specific examinations are held at your facility on your equipment and representative specimens. That is the point of the arrangement: the specific examination should test the procedures and acceptance criteria your technicians really use, whether those come from a rolling mill specification, a technical order or a customer drawing.

If you do not yet have a written practice, or yours predates your current methods, our Level III can build or review it. See written practice development and corporate NDT training, or ask about training a Spokane crew.

For Spokane candidates the practical examination is hands-on with real equipment and specimens and is never conducted remotely. If you want help writing the Level III side of the programme, see outsourced Level III consulting.

Radiography licensing in Washington

Washington is an NRC Agreement State, and the Department of Health's radioactive materials program licenses industrial radiography sources there. A radiography company needs its own licence, and each radiographer must meet the training, examination and supervision requirements in that licence and the state radiation rules. That is separate from method certification. An RT course from any provider, including this one, does not license a radiographer and does not authorise anyone to use a source. Spokane employers normally need both: radiation safety training and authorisation under the company licence, and SNT-TC-1A certification covering technique and interpretation. If you plan to work as a radiographer, confirm the current requirements directly with the Washington Department of Health.

Practise before your practical exam

The Practical NDT browser simulator lets a Spokane technician rehearse set-ups, scanning coverage and interpretation in virtual workplaces between hands-on sessions, and the NDT practice tests cover the general and method theory. They are rehearsal tools. They do not replace hands-on training, logged experience or the practical examination on real specimens under your employer's written practice.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, an ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT with more than eleven years of international field experience. He sets course content, oversees examinations, and reviews written practices and procedures for employer clients.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Spokane

How long does NDT training take in Spokane?

It depends on the method, the level and your employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours, and the experience hours usually take longest. The training-requirements matrix shows the recommended figures by method.

Where can I get NDT certified near Spokane?

Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you, so the route runs through an employer that has a written practice. Atlantis NDT provides the training and Level III support online and at the employer's site, and prepares candidates for ASNT central certification as an alternative.

Can I do NDT training online in Washington?

Yes, for the theory portion. The practical work is hands-on at an employer's facility or in the simulator for rehearsal.

Which NDT method should I learn first for work in Spokane?

Visual and magnetic particle or penetrant testing are the usual starting points, and they feed into ultrasonic work. Spokane's mix of fabrication, metals and power work uses all of them.

Is there demand for NDT technicians around Spokane?

The area has military aircraft support, aluminium production, utilities and fabrication, all of which use NDT. Postings change, so check employer career pages and talk to local fabricators directly.

Does an Atlantis course certify me?

No. A course provides training hours and examination preparation. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies. If you want ASNT central certification instead, we prepare you for that route.

Do the published fees on the page include the practical?

The published US fees on this page show what each course includes. Practical arrangements depend on your employer's facility, so ask us when you enquire.

Can I get Level III training in Spokane?

Yes. Level III preparation is self-paced online with Level III Q&A, covering the basic and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

Will my certificate transfer if I change employers?

An SNT-TC-1A certificate belongs to the employer that issued it. A new employer will usually re-examine you or accept your records under its own written practice. ASNT central certification travels with you.

Are there other training pages near Spokane?

Yes. Nearby markets with their own guides include Seattle, Portland, Billings, Idaho Falls, and the Washington training page covers the state as a whole.
